claims.statement: The security route's `+page.server.ts` load is deliberately shell-first: it validates the `security_id` param (throwing a 400 `Security ID is required` when absent) and returns only `{ security_id }`, never fetching the security identity or its price series on the server.

`SecurityPageDataService.load()` in `page-data.svelte.ts` increments a private `loadSeq` and discards its own result whenever a newer soft navigation has started, so a slow in-flight request cannot clobber a newer load; the `finally` block only clears `isLoading` for the newest sequence.

`SecurityPageDataService.load()` fetches the security identity and the `1d` price series in parallel via `Promise.all` inside a `getChartDateWindow(new SvelteDate(), '1d')` window, treats a missing or empty `items` array as a successful load whose message `No price data available for this security` lands in `error`, and never throws — it returns the caught error object so the caller can route a 401 through `redirectOn401`.

The titlebar resolves instantly: `security` is derived as `pageData.security ?? instantSecurity`, where `instantSecurity` is a lookup of `data.security_id` inside the already-loaded `watchlistService.defaultWatchlistSecurities`; a direct load with no watchlist entry falls back to the app-header skeleton until the data wave lands.

A single `$effect` keyed on `data.security_id` drives the post-mount init chain: it resets drawing tool state and pagination flags, awaits `pageData.load()`, loads user preferences, maps the `1d` items into candles, fans out `loadAlerts`/`loadHoldings`/`loadValuation`/`drawingsService.loadSnapshots` in parallel, dynamically imports `security-chart.svelte`, and force-refetches the active timeframe when it is not `1d`; the whole chain is try/caught so a failure in the import, preference or snapshot step cannot surface as an unhandled rejection.

The initial-load wave-alert reconcile is gated on `userPreferences !== null`, so a failed preference fetch can never mass-delete the user's wave alerts; the reconcile itself is serialized onto a single promise chain because `onWaveChange` fires per point while drawing and concurrent runs reading a stale `alerts` array would double-create, and reconcile failures are swallowed so drawing never breaks.

Price alerts are per-user rows in `market_price_alerts` with a `source` column constrained to `manual` or `wave`, defaulting to `manual` both in `PriceAlertWrite` and in the route (a chart-drawn or sidebar-created alert omits `source`); the page and the chart share the same `alerts` array, and `handleCreateAlert`/`handleDeleteAlert` re-run `loadAlerts()` after each mutation.

Notes and documents are per-user rows in `market_security_notes` and `market_security_documents`, and every related repository method (`get_by_security_and_user`, `delete`) filters on the authenticated `user.id`; the security identity itself is NOT user-scoped, since `market_get_security` looks it up by id alone.

Note creation and update write the row, return it immediately with `title` still null, and only then enqueue `generate_note_title_task` with the note id, so the HTTP request path never depends on the AI provider; the Huey task reloads the note, calls `ai_service.generate_note_title(note.content)` and writes the title back via `update_title`.

Document upload writes real bytes to local disk: `market_create_document` builds the directory from `Path(settings.upload_path)` (default `data/uploads`), `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`, names the file `f"{uuid.uuid4()}{ext}"`, writes the awaited `file.read()` to it, and only then stores a metadata row whose `file_path` is the absolute local path — a single-container assumption with no object storage.

Document deletion removes only the database row: `market_delete_document` calls `repository.delete(doc_id, user.id)`, whose implementation is a single `delete(SecurityDocumentModel).where(id).where(user_id)` plus commit, with no `unlink` or filesystem cleanup anywhere in the delete path — so deleting a document permanently orphans its bytes under `settings.upload_path`.

The document download path has no matching backend route in this checkout: `documentsService.downloadDocument` calls `getBlob('/market/securities/{security_id}/documents/{documentId}/download')` and `document-list-item.svelte` invokes it from the download button, but `market_router` declares only the GET, POST and DELETE document routes and no file in `src/` contains the string `download`.

Document upload validation is client-side only: `document-upload-dialog.svelte` rejects file types outside `application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `text/plain` and caps size at 10 MB, while the backend accepts any `UploadFile` without a type or size check; because `market_get_documents` returns a bare list rather than a paginated envelope, `DocumentsGroup` reads the response as an array while notes and alerts read `.items`.

`IndicatorsGroup` is the only fully bidirectional sidebar group and treats the persisted preference, not the page's `indicatorConfigs`, as the source of truth for the enabled flag (the page copy is stale after a sidebar toggle); it writes the merged `indicators` map with `patchPreferences` before awaiting the network to avoid lost-update races, and `resetSettings` restores color/numeric defaults while deliberately preserving the enabled state.

`HoldingsGroup` reads the user's account holdings for the security and derives a `% of Portfolio` figure by summing `accountClient.getAccountTotals` across every account; its average-price checkbox both toggles the chart overlay through `onToggleAveragePrice` and persists the `avgPrice` indicator preference, while the page independently computes `averageBuyingPrice = blendedAverageCost(holdings)` and passes it to the chart as `averagePrice`.

`FundamentalsGroup` binds the page's `valuation` and `showOverlay` state: `valuationClient.getValuation` maps a 404 to `null` so 'no range set' is a normal state rather than an error, the overlay checkbox persists `show_valuation_band` via `patchPreferences`, and the same state is threaded into `security-chart.svelte` as `valuation`/`showValuation`/`showValuationBand`; the backend stores it as a per-user row upserted by `PUT /market/securities/{security_id}/valuation`.

`AIAnalysisGroup` owns no persisted state: it is a three-entry action list (`fundamentals`, `summarize-notes`, `portfolio-debate`) where each action opens a response modal in a loading state, calls the matching `aiService` method, and writes `content` or `error` into the modal data; `portfolio-debate` currently sends the hardcoded placeholder context `'Analyzing in isolation for now.'`.

The route composes seven sidebar groups in a fixed order (Your Holdings, Fundamentals, Indicators, Price Alerts, Notes, Documents, AI Analysis) inside a `w-64` column; self-loading groups receive `expanded`, and groups that consume page-owned state (alerts, valuation/overlay, indicator configs, average-price visibility) are wired by bindable prop and callback rather than owning that state themselves.

The route's frontend test suite is contract-bound to mocking: it mocks every API client and network-touching module (`marketService`, `userPreferencesService`, `alertsService`, `notesService`, `documentsService`, `accountService`, `valuationClient`, `snapshotsService`, `watchlistService`, `$app/navigation`, `$app/paths`) plus the `Path2D` and `ResizeObserver` globals, and its `Instant Shell with Async Chart Data` block pins the shell-first behavior, timeframe force-refetch, error-card, 401-redirect and no-unhandled-rejection invariants.
